λυγρὰ: λυγρός — grievous, baneful, miserable; neut. acc. pl. (grave, mid-clause form): ’grievous things’
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέγαν: μέγας — great, big, tall; masc. acc. sg.
μέλαιναν: μέλας — black, dark; fem. acc. sg., agreeing with κῆρα · also agreeing with νῆα (θοὴν ἀνὰ νῆα μέλαιναν ’the swift black ship’) · also standing for a noun left out: ’a black (ewe)’ (θῆλύν τε μέλαιναν)
μένεϊ: μένος — might, force, fury; neut. dat. sg., epic -εϊ (= Attic -ει), object of ἐπισπόμενοι (‘following’): ‘their own might’
μή: μή — not; negative particle (used with imperatives and subjunctives, unlike οὐ) · also introducing a negative purpose/fear clause with the optative in secondary sequence: μή ἑ λάθοι ’lest he should escape notice’ · also μή + fut. inf. after a verb of swearing/promising, negating its content: μή ... βουλευσέμεν ’that ... will not plan’ · also ’lest’ with the subj. after a primary verb (μή πώς ... χαλεπήνῃ ’lest he be harsh’) · also in a question expecting the answer ’no’, after ἦ: ἦ μή … φάσθ’ ἔμμεναι; ’surely you do not say … are?’ · also ’lest’ + subj. after a past verb of urging (κελόμην … μή … λάθηται ’I urged … lest he forget’) · also in a condition, ’if … not’ (εἰ … μή τίς σε βιάζεται) · also with an infinitive used as an imperative, a prohibition: μή μ’ … καταλείπειν ’do not leave me’ · also negating a purpose clause after ἵνα: ’so that … not’ (ἵνα μή τι … ἀλγήσετε ’so that you may not suffer’) · also with the optative, a negative wish: ’may … not’ (μή … ἀντιβολήσαις) · also ὡς ἂν μή + subj., negative purpose: ’so that … not’ (ὡς ἂν μή σε κατατρύχῃ ’so that he may not wear you out’) · also + subj. giving the content of an oath, ’that no one …’ (ὀμόσσατε … μή τις … πλήξῃ ’swear that no one strike’) · also μή + subj. standing alone as a warning, ’lest’ (μή τίς τοι … ἀναστῇ ’lest someone rise up against you’) · also μή + fut. indic. in a fear clause: ’lest, I fear’ (μή τίς … νεμεσήσεται ’lest anyone resent’)
μήσατο: μήδομαι — devise, contrive, plan; aor. mid. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic ἐμήσατο)
μίμνετ: μένω — wait, stay, abide; pres. imper. 2 pl., reduplicated stem μίμνω, elided (μίμνετ’ = μίμνετε)
μακρά: μακρός — long, tall, high; neut. nom./acc. pl. (κύματα μακρά ’long waves’)
μεγάλῃ: μέγας — great, big; fem. dat. sg.
μεγάροις: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. pl.: ‘in the halls’
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μελαίνῃ: μέλας — black; standing epithet of ships; fem. dat. sg. μέλαινα · also modifying a different noun, not a ship (μελαίνῃ φρικί ’with a dark ripple’, of the sea’s surface)
μερμήριξε: μερμηρίζω — ponder, devise, turn over in the mind; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐμερμήριξε)
μετέειπε: μετεῖπον — speak among, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (= Attic μετεῖπε)
μεταμώνια: μεταμώνιος — wasted, vain, gone to the winds; neut. nom. pl.
μηδ: μηδέ — and not, nor; neg. conj., elided (μηδ’ = μηδέ)
μηνῶν: μείς (epic μήν) — month; masc. gen. pl., in a gen. absolute with φθινόντων
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μνηστήρεσσι: μνηστήρ — suitor; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσι
μνηστῆρες: μνηστήρ — suitor; nom. pl. · also masc. voc. pl., in address: ’suitors!’
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of the person affected, ’from my …’ (μοι βλεφάρων ἐξέσσυτο ὕπνος ’sleep rushed out from my eyelids’) · also dat. of possession with εἰμί: ’who are mine’ (οἵ μοι ἔασιν ’who are mine’)
μοῖρ: μοῖρα — fate, portion, lot; fem. nom. sg., elided (μοῖρ’ = μοῖρα)
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses · also negating a conditional clause after εἰ: εἰ μὴ ’if not, unless’ · also negating a generic relative clause with the opt.: ὃς μὴ … ἐλάσειε ’whoever did not drive off’ · also ’lest’ in a warning, + 2 sg. fut./subj.: μὴ … ἀποτίσεαι ’lest you pay for it’ · also + inf., negating an infinitive of advice that gives the content of a word: ’not to’ (ἔπος … μὴ πάντα μνηστῆρσιν ὁμιλεῖν ’a word, not to mingle in everything with the suitors’) · also negating a generic relative clause with the subj.: ᾧ μὴ πολλοὶ ἔωσιν ’who has not many’
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg. · also a plan, scheme agreed on (τοῖον...τελέωμεν μῦθον ’let us carry out this plan’)
νήεσσι: ναῦς — ship; fem. dat. pl., epic νήεσσι (= Attic ναυσί)
νήματ: νῆμα — thread, spun yarn; neut. nom. pl., elided (νήματ’ = νήματα)
ναῖε: ναίω — dwell, inhabit, live; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔναιε): ’was dwelling, used to live’
νεμεσήσῃ: νεμεσάω — feel righteous indignation; aor. subj. 3 sg.
νευρὴν: νευρή — bowstring, cord; fem. acc. sg.
νηῒ: ναῦς — ship; fem. dat. sg., epic νηΐ (diaeresis marks the two syllables)
νηῶν: ναῦς — ship; fem. gen. pl., epic νηῶν (= Attic νεῶν)
νόσφι: νόσφι — apart from, except (+ gen.); adv./prep.
νύκτας: νύξ — night; fem. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’by nights’
ξεῖνος: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); nom. sg.
οἰχομένοιο: οἴχομαι — be gone, have gone away; pres. part. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), perfect sense: ’gone’
οἰῶν: ὄϊς (Attic οἶς) — sheep; masc./fem. gen. pl., contracted (= epic ὀίων)
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’) · also article-like with a numeral and noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’the’ (οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι ’the two crags’) · also encl. dat. sg. of a thing, ’to/for it’ (δύω δέ τέ οἱ θύραι ’and it has two doors’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’those, the’ (οἱ πέπλοι ’the robes’) · also dat. sg. of the giver with δέχομαι: ’from him’ (οἱ ἐδέξατο ’took from him’)
οἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl. · also encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (= οἱ, accented οἵ in this position) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; masc. nom. pl. ’they’, demonstrative: οἵ γ’ ὑβρισταί ’are they violent?’
οἶος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg.
οἷον: οἷος — such as, of what sort; neut. as exclamatory adv.: ’how!, what a thing!’ (rough breathing; distinct from οἶος ’alone’) · also causal conj. after a verb of emotion, ’in that, that’ · also correlative ’such as, as’ (οἷον ὅτε πρώτιστον ’such as when first’) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with τὸν Τηλεφίδην: ’what a man, such a one as’ (ἀλλ’ οἷον … κατενήρατο ’but what a man he slew’) · also neut. acc. sg. agreeing with ἦμαρ: ’of such a kind as’ (οἷον ἐπ’ ἦμαρ ἄγησι ’such as the day he brings’) · also neut. nom./acc. sg., agreeing with μένος: ’what sort of (strength)’
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὐχ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a rough breathing (οὐχ)
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also masc. acc. sg.: ’all’ (πάντα δῆμον ’all the people’) · also neut. acc. pl. adverbial: ’altogether, in every respect’ (οὐκ ἄρα πάντα νοήμονες ’not altogether sensible’)
πάντες: πᾶς — all, every; masc. nom. pl.
πάντη: πάντῃ — on every side, in every direction; adv. (Ionic -η)
πέλεν: πέλω — be, become; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented: ’was’
παθόντες: πάσχω — suffer, experience; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having suffered’
παπταίνων: παπταίνω — look about, peer around; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
παραθεῖτο: παρατίθημι — set beside, place before; aor. opt. mid. 3 sg., in a clause of repeated circumstance
περίμετρον: περίμετρος — very large, of great compass (περί ’exceedingly’ + μέτρον ’measure’); masc. acc. sg.
περικαλλέα: περικαλλής — very beautiful; fem. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic περικαλλῆ) · also neut. nom./acc. pl., agreeing with a neuter plural noun: ’very beautiful’ (ἔργα ... περικαλλέα ’very beautiful works, fine handiwork’) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with δίφρον: ‘very fair (stool)’
περικλυτόν: περικλυτός — famed all round, far-renowned; neut. acc. sg.
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’) · also + gen., of place, physically ’around, encircling’ (περὶ σπείους γλαφυροῖο ’around the hollow cave’), distinct from the comparative ’beyond’ sense above · also + dat. in the fixed idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περὶ κῆρι τιμήσουσιν ’will honor him at heart’) · also + dat., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ χροῒ ’about the skin’) · also adverb of place, no case: ’round about’ (περὶ δ’ ἕρκος ἐλήλαται ’and round it a fence is driven’) · also + dat., of the thing fought over: ’over, for’ (περὶ κτεάτεσσι μαχειόμενος ’fighting over possessions’) · also + gen., of the thing fought over: ’over, for’ (fighting over a person)
πηνελοπείῃ: Πηνελόπεια — Penelope; dat. sg., dat. of comparison · also dat. sg., indirect object: ’to Penelope’ (ἐρέοντα περίφρονι Πηνελοπείῃ ’to tell prudent Penelope’) · also dat. sg. in apposition to a preceding dative of the person affected: ’(the daughter of Icarius,) prudent Penelope’
ποθεν: πόθεν — from somewhere; indefinite enclitic adv. (accentless after εἰ), distinct from interrogative πόθεν ’from where?’
πολιόν: πολιός — grey, hoary; masc. acc. sg. (also neut. nom./acc. sg.)
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’ · also neut. nom. pl., plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun (πολλὰ ... δάκρυα ’many tears’) · also neut. acc. pl., plain attributive adj. (κτήματα πολλὰ ’many possessions’) · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’again and again’ (πολλὰ περιτροπέοντες) · also neut. nom. pl. as substantive, subject: οἷά τε πολλὰ γίγνεται ’as many things happen’
πολλὸν: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, epic (= Attic πολύ): ’much’ · also attributive, neut. nom. sg. agreeing with μέθυ: ’much (wine)’ · also neut. acc. sg. as substantive object: ’much (wine)’ · also adj.: ’big’ · also epic πολλόν (= πολύν), masc. acc. sg., agreeing with χρόνον: ’long (time)’
πολυμήχαν: πολυμήχανος — many-devising; voc. sg., elided (πολυμήχαν’ = πολυμήχανε)
πολύτλας: πολύτλας — much-enduring; adj., masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Odysseus (πολύ ’much’ + root of τλῆναι ’endure’)
ποσειδάων: Ποσειδῶν — Poseidon, god of the sea, enemy of Odysseus after the blinding of his son Polyphemus; nom. sg., epic uncontracted · also elided acc. sg., Ποσειδάων’ = Ποσειδάωνα: ’Poseidon’ as object
ποτ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv., elided (ποτ’ = ποτέ)
προσεφώνεεν: προσφωνέω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεφώνει)
προτὶ: πρός (epic by-form προτί) — towards, to; prep. + acc. · also adverb ’besides, in addition’, or preverb in tmesis: ’in, to (oneself)’ (προτὶ … ἐκάλεσσας = προσεκάλεσσας ’called in’)
πρόσθ: πρόσθε — before, in front of; prep. + gen., elided (πρόσθ’ = πρόσθε) · also adv., ’ahead, in front’ (πρόσθ’ ἡγεμόνευεν ’led the way in front’)
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ ’be dashed against the floor’) · also + dat., ’in addition to’ (πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος ’and sleep in addition to these’) · also + gen., of direction: ’toward, on the side of’ (πρὸς Βορέαο ’toward the North Wind’) · also + gen., in an appeal: ’by (your father)’ (πρὸς πατρὸς γουνάζομαι) · also as preverb in tmesis: με πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε = με προσέειπε μῦθον ’spoke a word to me’ · also + gen., ’in the eyes of, with’ (πρὸς πόσιός τε καὶ υἱέος ’in the eyes of her husband and son’)
πτολίπορθον: πτολίπορθος — sacker of cities (Attic πολίπορθος); masc. acc. sg., epithet of Odysseus
πτόλιν: πτόλις (epic by-form of πόλις) — city; acc. sg.
πτόλιος: πτόλις (epic for πόλις) — city; fem. gen. sg. (= Attic πόλεως)
πω: πω — yet, up to now; enclitic adv., usu. with a negative
πόληος: πόλις — city; gen. sg., epic (= Attic πόλεως)
πόλιος: πόλις — city; fem. gen. sg., epic (= Attic πόλεως)
πόλλ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl., elided (πόλλ’ = πολλά): ’many’ · also used adverbially: ‘much, often’ (πόλλ’ ἐπέεσσιν ‘again and again with words’) · also neut. nom. pl., attributive: ’many’ (ἤματα πόλλ’ ’many days’)
πόντον: πόντος — sea, open sea; acc. sg.
πόσιν: πόσις — husband; acc. sg. · also the distinct noun πόσις ’a drinking, drink’ (from πίνω); acc. sg.: ’drink’ (paired with βρῶσις ’eating’)
πύλου: Πύλος — Pylos, city in the Peloponnese, home of Nestor; gen. sg.
πώεα: πῶυ — flock (of sheep); neut. acc. pl., epic uncontracted
σκηπτόμενον: σκήπτομαι — lean on, support oneself on; pres. part. mid. masc. acc. sg.: ’leaning (on a staff)’
σοὶ: σύ — you (sg.); dat. sg.: ’to, for you’
σπείρου: σπεῖρον — cloth, wrapping, winding-sheet; neut. gen. sg.
σπουδῇ: σπουδή — haste, effort, zeal; fem. dat. sg. used adverbially: ‘with effort, barely’ · also fem. dat. sg. adverbial, ’in haste, hurriedly’ (σπουδῇ νῦν ἀνάβαινε ’now go aboard in haste’)
στησαμένη: ἵστημι — set up, set; aor. part. mid. fem. nom. sg.: ’having set up (for herself)’
στονόεντα: στονόεις — full of groaning, grievous; neut. acc. pl., epic -όεντα
στυγερὴ: στυγερός — hateful, loathsome; fem. nom. sg., agreeing with νοῦσος
στυγερὸν: στυγερός — hateful, loathsome; masc. acc. sg.
στόνος: στόνος — groaning, moaning; masc. nom. sg.
στῆ: ἵστημι — set, stand; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔστη): ’stood’
σφι: σφι — epic dat. pl. pron. ’to/for them’ (= Attic αὐτοῖς)
σφῷ: σφός — their own; neut. dat. sg., epic possessive adj. of the 3rd person (not a relative), agreeing with μένεϊ: ‘their own’
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat. · also as adverb, ’together’, or as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: σὺν … κάλυψε = συνεκάλυψε ’covered up’; σὺν … ἔπεσον = συνέπεσον ’fell together, clashed’ · also adverb ’along, with (us)’ construed with ἔχοντες, which takes the object (σὺν … χεῖρας ἔχοντες ’having hands along with us’)
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’ · also after ἤ ’than’, with no connective force: ἤ τ’ οἰωνοί ’than birds’ · also after ὅ ‘that’, with no connective force: ὅ τ’ οὐκέτι νόστιμός ἐστιν ‘that he is no longer returning’
τάδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also with a noun, neut. acc. pl.: ’these’ (τάδε δώμαθ’ ’this house’, plural for one dwelling)
τέλος: τέλος — end, completion, fulfilment; neut. nom./acc. sg.
τέτρατον: τέταρτος — fourth; epic by-form τέτρατος, neut. nom. sg. (agreeing with ἔτος)
τήν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg., resumptive: ’whom’ · also demonstrative, fem. acc. sg., resuming an earlier noun: ’her’ (τήν … ῥέξω ’her I will sacrifice’) · also relative, fem. acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὀιζυῖ πολλῇ, τήν μοι ἐπῶρσε ’great misery, which he roused for me’) · also demonstrative with a noun and adjective: ’that’ (τήν γε στυγερὴν ὁδόν ’that hateful journey’)
τί: τίς, τί — who? what?; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially ’why’ · also the enclitic indefinite τις, τι ’someone, something’ (accented τί before an enclitic): neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a negative, ’at all’ (οὔ τι) · adj. · also plain interrogative, direct object/predicate: ’what’ (τί πάθω ’what am I to suffer’; τί ... γένηται ’what is to become’) · also the enclitic indefinite as an adjective agreeing with a noun, accented before enclitic που: εἴ τί που εἴλυμα ’if any wrapper’ · also enclitic indefinite with a negative, ’anything’, as accusative subject of an infinitive (οὐ … τί φημι κακώτερον ἄλλο … συγχεῦαι ’I say nothing else is worse’) · also enclitic indefinite, adverbial without a negative: ’somehow, in some way’ (τοῦτό τί μοι κάλλιστον ’this seems to me somehow the fairest’) · also enclitic indefinite as an adjective after μή, accented before an enclitic: ’any’ (μή τί τοι … πῆμα ’any harm to you’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ὅπως, accented before enclitic μοι: ’any’ (τί … ἄλγος ’any pain’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ἤ, accented before the enclitic μοι: ’any’ (ἤ τί μοι … κειμήλιον ’or any treasure of mine’) · also the enclitic indefinite as a substantive object after εἴ: ’anything’ (εἴ τί μιν εἴποι ’whether she would say anything to him’)
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
τανηλεγέος: τανηλεγής — meaning unknown (traditionally ’laying at full length’ or ’bringing long sorrow’), epithet of death; masc./fem. gen. sg.
ταφήϊον: ταφήϊος — of burial, for a funeral; neut. acc. sg. as noun: ’burial-shroud’ (Attic ταφήιος)
ταχέας: ταχύς — swift; masc. acc. pl., epic -έας (= Attic ταχεῖς), agreeing with ὀϊστούς: ’swift’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τετληότι: τλάω — endure, have the heart to bear; perf. part. (τετληώς) masc./neut. dat. sg.: ’enduring’
τετυγμένον: τεύχω — make, fashion, construct; perf. pass. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’wrought, well-made’
τεύξουσι: τεύχω — make, make ready, prepare; fut. 3 pl.
τεύχε: τεῦχος — armour, gear (pl. τεύχεα); neut. acc. pl., elided (τεύχε’ = τεύχεα)
τηλέμαχος: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; nom. sg.
τηλεμάχῳ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. dat. sg.
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg. · also with a negative: ’any, anyone’ (οὐ … τις ’no one’; οὐδέ τις ’nor any’) · also after the relative ὅς, indefinite: ὅς τις ’whichever, whoever’
τιτυσκόμενος: τιτύσκομαι — aim at, take aim; pres. part. mid. masc. nom. sg., reduplicated: ’aiming’
τοί: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl. ’they’ · also relative: ’who’ · also encl. dat. sg. pron. σύ ’to you’ (= τοι, accented before a following enclitic, e.g. τοί τι) · also τοι, the affirming particle, accented τοί before an enclitic: ἀλλ’ ἦ τοί σε ’but truly you’
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοιαῦτα: τοιοῦτος — such, of such a kind; demonstr. pron./adj., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’such things’
τοὶ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl.: ’they’; also relative: ’who’ · also τοι, the affirming particle (ἀλλ’ ἦ τοι ’but truly’), as the grave-accented form τοὶ
τρίετες: τρίετες — for three years; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially (acc. of duration), from τρίετης
τυπτομένων: τύπτω — strike, beat; pres. part. pass. gen. pl.: ’being struck’
τόνδ: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstr. pron., masc. acc. sg., elided (τόνδ’ = τόνδε)
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. nom. pl. (μῆλα, τὰ … κατάκειτ’ ’the flocks, which lie’) · also relative, neut. acc. pl.: ’which’, object of the verb in its clause (ῥωγαλέα, τὰ … ὅρηαι ’torn, which you see’) · also article-like with a substantivized adjective, neut.: ’the (worse things)’ (τὰ χέρεια) · also neut. acc. pl. ’them’, of the cow and the goats · also article-like before an adverb, ’the (things) outside’ (τὰ θύρηφι)
τὸ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg. (τὸ πάροιθεν ’that which was before’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’that, the’ (τὸ σῆμα ’that mark’) · also article-like before the adverb πάρος: ’as before’ (ὡς τὸ πάρος περ) · also article-like before an ordinal, adverbial: τὸ τρίτον ’the third time’ · also distributive, neut. nom./acc. sg.: τὸ μὲν … τὸ δὲ ’one thing … another’ · also article-like before the adverb πρόσθεν: ’formerly’ (τὸ πρόσθεν ὄλοντο ’died long before’) · also article-like before a substantivized adjective, neut.: τὸ μέλαν ’the dark (part)’ · also article-like before the adverb πάροιθε: ’formerly’ (τὸ πάροιθε ’in former times’) · also article-like before an infinitive, which it makes a noun: ’the (keeping watch)’ (τὸ φυλάσσειν) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. acc. sg., object of its clause (τὸ πρὶν μέν ῥ’ ἐφόρει ’which he used to carry before’) · also demonstrative, neut. acc. sg., object of a verb: ’this, that’ (τὸ δὲ νήπιοι οὐκ ἐνόησαν ’but the fools did not perceive this’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’) · also demonstrative, distributive: masc. acc. sg. ’the one … the other’ (τὸν μὲν … τὸν δ’) · also article-like with a participle: τὸν ἐόντα ’me, the one who am’ · also article-like with a superlative or ordinal: ’the best’ (τὸν ἄριστον), ’the fourth’ (τὸν τέταρτον) · also article-like with a substantivized adjective: ’the like (one)’ (τὸν ὁμοῖον)
τὼ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. dual: ’the two of them’  ·  also acc. dual, object of a verb of address: τὼ … προσέφη ’spoke to the two of them’ · also relative, nom. dual, ’who (the two)’: τοκῆε δύω, τὼ μὴ γείνασθαι ὄφελλον · also nom. dual with a noun, article-like: ’the two’ (τὼ … θεράποντε)
τῆος: τῆος — meanwhile, for so long; adv., epic (= Attic τέως), correlative of ἧος
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’ · also with a noun, article-like: τῶν ἄλλων ἀνέμων ’of the other winds’ · also distributive, ’of the one … of the other’ (τῶν μὲν … τῶν δ’ ’of the one band … of the other’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: gen. pl. ’of whom, whose’ (τῶν ὕβρις τε βίη τε … ἵκει ’whose insolence and violence reach’)
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’) · also demonstrative instrumental, of a thing just named: ’with it’ (τῷ ἀπὸ πείσματ’ ἔκοψα ’with it I cut the cables off’) · also demonstrative of a thing just named, before a preposition: ’it’ (τῷ δ’ ἐν ’and on it’, τῷ δ’ ὑπό ’and beneath it’) · also adverbial, with κε: ’in that case, otherwise’ (τῷ κέ μιν … παύσαμεν ’otherwise we should have stopped him’)
υἱέϊ: υἱός — son; masc. dat. sg., epic υἱέϊ (= Attic υἱῷ)
φίλα: φίλος — dear, one’s own; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially with φρονέω: ’with friendly thoughts, kindly’ · also plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun: ’dear’ (τέκνα φίλα ’dear children’) · also neut. acc. pl. as substantive, object: ’dear things, kindnesses’ (φίλα ἔρδοι ’may do kindnesses’)
φίλοι: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. nom. pl.: ’dear (guest-friends)’ · also masc. voc. pl. (identical form), direct address: ’friends!’ (δεῦτε, φίλοι) · also attributive, with a noun: φίλοι υἷες ’dear sons’
φίλος: φίλος — dear, dear one; masc. nom. sg. used as voc.: ’friend’ · also plain attributive adjective, not vocative: ’dear’ (φίλος υἱός ’dear son’) · also predicate adjective: ’dear’ (φίλος ἦεν Ἰήσων ’Jason was dear (to her)’)
φθινόντων: φθίνω — waste away, wane, dwindle; pres. part. masc. gen. pl.: ’waning’
φρένες: φρήν — mind, heart, midriff (seat of feeling); fem. nom. pl.
φρεσὶ: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. dat. pl.
φόνου: φόνος — killing, slaughter; masc. gen. sg.
φᾶρος: φᾶρος — large cloth, robe, web; neut. acc. sg.
φῆμιν: φῆμις (Ionic-epic φήμη) — report, talk of people, rumour; fem. acc. sg.
χέρσου: χέρσος — dry land, shore; fem. gen. sg., with ἐπί: ’on the shore’
χαρίεσσαν: χαρίεις — graceful, pleasing, gracious; fem. acc. sg. χαρίεσσαν
χροῒ: χρώς — skin, flesh, the body’s surface; dat. sg. χροΐ
ψυχὴ: ψυχή — soul, spirit, ghost; fem. nom. sg.
ἀΐδαο: Ἀΐδης — Hades, god and realm of the dead; masc. gen. sg., epic -αο (= Attic Ἅιδου)
ἀέθλια: ἀέθλιον — prize, contest (epic; cf. Attic ἆθλον); neut. acc. pl. · also neut. nom. pl. (same form), in apposition to the subject: ἀέθλια τοῖο ἄνακτος ’prizes of that lord’
ἀγήνωρ: ἀγήνωρ — lordly, manly, proud; adj. (2-termination), masc./fem. nom. sg.
ἀγλαὸν: ἀγλαός — splendid, radiant, bright; masc./neut. acc. sg.
ἀγορεύεις: ἀγορεύω — speak out, declare, say; pres. 2 sg.
ἀγροῦ: ἀγρός — field, countryside; gen. sg. (ἐπ’ ἀγροῦ ’out in the country’) · also plain gen. sg. dependent on a noun, ’of the field/farmland’: ἀγροῦ ἐπ’ ἐσχατιήν ’to the edge of the farmland’
ἀγρὸν: ἀγρός — field, farmland, country; masc. acc. sg.
ἀγχιστῖνοι: ἀγχιστῖνος — close together, one upon another (sense inferred from ἄγχι); masc. nom. pl., epic
ἀγόρευον: ἀγορεύω — speak, say, declare; impf. 3 pl.
ἀείρας: ἀείρω — lift, raise (Attic αἴρω); aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having lifted’
ἀεικὴς: ἀεικής — unseemly, shameful; masc. nom. sg.
ἀθάνατοι: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. nom. pl.: ’the immortals’
ἀκηδέα: ἀκηδής — uncared for, neglected; neut. nom. pl., epic uncontracted (= ἀκηδῆ) · also neut. acc. pl., agreeing with an object: ’uncared-for (armour)’
ἀλλ: ἀλλά (elided ἀλλ’) — but; well then · also ’except’: ’but only’ (ἀλλ’ οἶοι ’except us two’)
ἀλλήλους: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., masc. acc. pl.
ἀλλύεσκεν: ἀναλύω — unravel, undo, unloose again; impf. 3 sg. iterative in -σκον, epic assimilated (ἀλλύεσκεν = ἀναλύεσκεν)
ἀλλύουσαν: ἀναλύω — unravel, undo; pres. part. fem. acc. sg., epic assimilated (ἀλλύουσαν = ἀναλύουσαν)
ἀνάγκης: ἀνάγκη — necessity, compulsion; fem. gen. sg.: ’under compulsion’
ἀνάρσιοι: ἀνάρσιος — hostile, unfriendly; masc. nom. pl.
ἀνθρώπους: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; acc. pl.
ἀντίνοον: Ἀντίνοος — Antinous, a leading suitor; masc. acc. sg.
ἀντιθέῳ: ἀντίθεος — godlike, a match for a god; masc. dat. sg.
ἀπωλόμεθ: ἀπόλλυμι — destroy; mid. perish; aor. mid. 1 pl., elided (ἀπωλόμεθ’ = ἀπωλόμεθα): ’we perished’
ἀρίστους: ἀγαθός — good; superlative ἄριστος, masc. acc. pl.: ’best’
ἀρετῆς: ἀρετή — excellence, worth (of a person); fem. gen. sg.
ἀρετῇ: ἀρετή — excellence, virtue, prowess; fem. dat. sg., dat. of respect: ’in excellence’
ἀρχήν: ἀρχή — beginning, first cause (also rule, office); fem. acc. sg.
ἀτρεΐδαο: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus, i.e. Agamemnon; gen. sg., epic (-αο = Attic -ου)
ἀτρεΐδη: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus; masc. voc. sg.
ἀτρεκέως: ἀτρεκής — exact, unswerving; adv. ἀτρεκέως: ’exactly, precisely’
ἀχαιούς: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. acc. pl.
ἀχαιϊάδων: Ἀχαιιάς — Achaean woman; fem. gen. pl.
ἄλλοις: ἄλλος — other, another; masc./neut. dat. pl.
ἄλλον: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. acc. sg.
ἄλλως: ἄλλως — otherwise, in another way; adv. · also ’idly, to no purpose, without ground’ (ἄλλως … ψεύδοντ’ ’tell lies idly’)
ἄλοχον: ἄλοχος — wife, one who shares the bed; acc. sg.
ἄναξ: ἄναξ — lord, master; masc. nom. sg. · also voc. sg. (same form), in address: ’lord!’ (κλῦθι, ἄναξ ’hear me, lord’)
ἄνδρες: ἀνήρ — man; nom. pl. · also masc. voc. pl., in address: ’men!’ (ἄνδρες, ἐπεὶ κνίση μὲν ἀνήνοθεν)
ἄντα: ἄντα — opposite, facing; adv. · also prep. + gen., ’in front of, before’: ἄντα παρειάων ’before her cheeks’
ἄνωγε: ἄνωγα — command, bid, order; perf. with pres./past force, 3 sg.: ’bade, had bidden’
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel · also the shortened form ἄρ used, without true elision, before τε in the fixed collocation ἄρ τε: τὰ μὲν ἄρ τε διεσκέδασ’ · also ἄρ before an elided κ’ (κε), ’then’, in a question: ἦ ἄρ κ’ ἐθέλοις ’would you then be willing?’ · also the shortened ἄρ before a consonant, without elision: ’then’ (ἐπεὶ ἄρ βλέφαρ’ … ἀμφικαλύψῃ ’when then (sleep) has covered the eyelids’) · also ἄρ before ἕζετ’ without elision: ’then’ (κατ’ ἄρ ἕζετ’ ’then sat down’)
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄστυ: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. sg.
ἄτερ: ἄτερ — without, apart from; prep. + gen.
ἅμ: ἅμα (elided ἅμ’) — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἅπαν: ἅπας — all, the whole; neut. nom. sg. (δάπεδον ἅπαν ’the whole floor’)
ἐδάμασσεν: δαμάζω — overpower, subdue, kill; aor. 3 sg., epic -σσ-, ν-movable (= Attic ἐδάμασε)
ἐδηλήσαντ: δηλέομαι — harm, hurt, injure; aor. 3 pl. mid., elided (ἐδηλήσαντ’ = ἐδηλήσαντο)
ἐθέλουσ: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing; pres. part. fem. nom. sg., elided, concessive (ἐθέλουσ’ = ἐθέλουσα): ’though unwilling’
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκέλευσεν: κελεύω — command, order, bid; aor. 3 sg.
ἐκτελέσω: ἐκτελέω — finish completely, accomplish; aor. subj. 1 sg.
ἐκχεύατ: ἐκχέω — pour out; aor. 3 sg. mid., elided (ἐκχεύατ’ = ἐκχεύατο), epic unaugmented (= Attic ἐξεχέατο): ’poured out’
ἐμοὶ: ἐγώ — I; dat. sg.: ’to, for me’ · also dat. of possession: ’mine is, I have’ (ἐμοὶ δ’ ὄνομα ’my name is’)
ἐμόγησεν: μογέω — toil, labor, suffer hardship; aor. 3 sg., augmented (ν-movable): ’toiled’
ἐμὸν: ἐμός — my, mine; masc./neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject: ’my’ (ὄνομ’ … ἐμὸν ’my name’; ἐμὸν κῆρ ’my heart’)
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐναλίγκιον: ἐναλίγκιος — like, resembling (+ dat.); masc. acc. sg., agreeing with the speaker: ’like (a beggar)’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with the object ἄνακτα: ’like (a beggar)’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with the relative ὅν (subject of εἶναι), + dat.: ’like (the gods)’ (θεοῖς ἐναλίγκιον)
ἐντανύσαι: ἐντανύω — stretch, string (a bow); aor. inf. act. (= Attic ἐντεῖναι)
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐξετέλεσσε: ἐκτελέω — bring to completion, finish; aor. 3 sg.
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’) · also + dat., of time: ’in, within’ (ἐπ’ ἤματι ’in a day’) · also + acc., ’in pursuit of, after’ (ἐπ’ ἀγροτέρας ’after wild (goats)’) · also + dat., ’in favour of, on behalf of’ (ἐπ’ Ἴρῳ ἦρα φέρων ’showing favour to Irus’) · also + acc. of time: ’for’ (ἐπ’ ἦμαρ ’for a day’) · also + gen., of place: ’at, on’ (ἐπ’ ἐσχατιῆς ’at the edge’) · also + dat., of place: ’at, by’ (ἐπ’ Ὠκεανῷ ’at Oceanus’)
ἐπέεσσι: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic ἔπεσι)
ἐπήλυθον: ἐπέρχομαι — come upon, come on, pass by; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= Attic ἐπῆλθον)
ἐπειγόμενοι: ἐπείγομαι — press on, be eager for, hasten; pres. part. masc. nom. pl. mid., + acc.: ’eager for’
ἐπεπείθετο: πείθω — persuade; plpf. 3 sg. with impf. sense: ’was won over’ · also ἐπιπείθομαι — obey (+ dat.); impf. 3 sg. mid., augment after the preverb (ἐπ-ε-πείθετο): ’obeyed’ (φίλῳ ἐπεπείθετο πατρί ’obeyed his dear father’)
ἐπιδευέες: ἐπιδευής — in want of, lacking (+ gen.); masc. nom. pl., epic uncontracted -έες (= Attic -εῖς)
ἐπισπόμενοι: ἕπομαι — follow; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ‘following’
ἐπιστροφάδην: ἐπιστροφάδην — turning this way and that, wheeling about; adv. (from ἐπιστρέφω)
ἐπιχθονίοισιν: ἐπιχθόνιος — on the earth, earthly; adj., masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἐποτρύνων: ἐποτρύνω — urge on, spur on; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’) · also adverb of sequence, ’next, thereupon’ (ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ ψυχή ’and next came the soul’) · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο = ἐπιτέταλτο ’was laid upon, entrusted’ · also + acc. of time: ’for, over’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + dat., ’in charge of, over’ (ἐπὶ κτεάτεσσιν ’over my possessions’) · also + dat., of purpose: ’for’ (ἐπὶ δόρπῳ ’for supper’) · also + dat., of the occasion: ’at, over’ (ἐπὶ ῥηθέντι δικαίῳ ’at a fair remark’)
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσχατιήν: ἐσχατιή — edge, border, outlying land; fem. acc. sg.
ἐτάνυσσε: τανύω — stretch, draw out; aor. 3 sg., double σ metrical
ἐτελέσθη: τελέω — bring to pass, accomplish, fulfil; aor. pass. 3 sg.: ’has been brought to pass’
ἐτύχθη: τεύχω — make, bring about; aor. pass. 3 sg.: ‘came to pass’
ἐφεύρομεν: ἐφευρίσκω — find, discover, catch (in the act); aor. 1 pl.
ἐχέφρονι: ἐχέφρων — sound-minded, prudent; fem. dat. sg.
ἐόντα: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc./neut. acc. sg., epic (= Attic ὄντα) · also neut. nom. pl., agreeing with θύρετρα ’doors’: καὶ εὐρέα περ ἐόντα ’wide though they are’
ἑκάστου: ἕκαστος — each, every; masc. gen. sg.
ἑσταότ: ἵστημι — set; stand; perf. part. masc. acc. sg., elided (ἑσταότ’ = ἑσταότα, Attic ἑστηκότα): ’standing’
ἔγειρε: ἐγείρω — rouse, wake; indic. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἤγειρε), aor. or impf. (the Attic form is the same for both): ’woke’ · also pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’wake!’
ἔδειξεν: δείκνυμι — show, point out; aor. 3 sg.
ἔειπε: εἶπον — say, speak, tell; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept before the root’s own ει- (= Attic εἶπε)
ἔειπεν: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. 3 sg., epic augmented (ἔ-ειπεν, = Attic εἶπεν)
ἔην: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἔληθε: λήθω (poetic by-form of λανθάνω) — escape notice, elude; impf. 3 sg., augmented, + dat. of means: ’escaped notice by’
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’) · also doubled, ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ’this way and that’
ἔπειθεν: πείθω — persuade, deceive; impf. 3 sg., augmented
ἔπειτ: ἔπειτα (elided ἔπειτ’) — then, next, after that
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἔφαθ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἔφατο, elided ἔφαθ’, τ>θ before rough breathing)
ἔχοντα: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. masc. acc. sg.: ‘holding’ · also with ἄλγεα, masc. acc. sg.: ’suffering, enduring’ (κρατέρ’ ἄλγε’ ἔχοντα ’beset by harsh pains’) · also of clothing, masc. acc. sg.: ’wearing’ (τοιάδε λαίφε’ ἔχοντα ’wearing such rags’)
ἔῃσιν: εἰμί — be; pres. subj. 3 sg., epic -ῃσιν (= Attic ᾖ): ’he may be, he is’
ἕπεσθαι: ἕπομαι — follow, accompany, go with; pres. inf.: ’to go with, accompany’
ἕστο: ἕννυμι — clothe; mid. put on, wear; plpf. 3 sg. mid., epic, + acc.: ’he was wearing, he had put on’
ἠελίῳ: ἥλιος — sun; masc. dat. sg., epic ἠέλιος (= Attic ἥλιος)
ἠμαθόεντος: ἠμαθόεις — sandy (epithet of Pylos); masc. gen. sg.
ἠματίη: ἠμάτιος — by day, in the daytime; fem. nom. sg. used adverbially
ἠὲ: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ) · also introducing the first alternative of a question: ’whether’ (ἠὲ διεπράθετο … ἦ … ’whether it was sacked … or …’) · also ’than’, after a word of difference (ἀλλοῖος … ἠὲ πάροιθεν ’different than before’) · also ’than’ after a comparative or word of preference (βέλτερόν ἐστι … ἠὲ ’it is better … than’) · also introducing the first alternative of a command: ’either’ (ἠὲ σὺ πρῶτος ἔσελθε ’either you go in first’)
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’ · also fem. nom. sg. ’it’, of a pool of water (ἡ δὲ προσέπλαζε ’and it lapped up’) · also fem. nom. sg. ’it’, of a ship (ἡ δ’ ἔθει ’and it ran’) · also fem. nom. sg. with a noun/adj., article-like: ’the other’ (ἡ δ’ ἄλλη ’and the other woman’) · also fem. nom. sg. article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ἡ γὰρ δμώων δίκη ’for the way of servants’) · also fem. nom. sg. ’it’, of a bowstring (ἡ δ’ ὑπὸ καλὸν ἄεισε ’and it sang beautifully’)
ἡγεμόνευε: ἡγεμονεύω — lead the way, be the guide (+ dat.); impf. 3 sg. (augment not visible on ἡ-) · also pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’lead the way!’
ἡμετέρου: ἡμέτερος — our; masc. gen. sg., agreeing with οἴκου
ἡμεῖς: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; nom. pl. ’we’
ἡμῖν: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; dat. pl. ’to us’
ἣ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
ἣν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (fem. acc. sg.)
ἤγαγε: ἄγω — lead, bring; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’led, brought’
ἤματα: ἦμαρ — day; neut. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’all the days, every day’ · also neut. nom. pl., subject: ’the days’ (νύκτες τε καὶ ἤματα φθίνουσιν)
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἥρωϊ: ἥρως — hero, warrior; masc. dat. sg., epic -ϊ (= Attic ἥρῳ), dat. of interest: ’for the hero’
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἦγε: ἄγω — lead, bring; impf. 3 sg.: ’led, brought’
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἦλθεν: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’came’
ἧκε: ἵημι — send, let go, let fall; aor. 3 sg. (with κὰδ in tmesis: ’let down’) · also of hurling a missile: ’hurled’ (ἧκε … κορυφὴν ὄρεος ’hurled the peak of a mountain’) · also with ἐν in tmesis: ’put in’ (ἐν … ἧκε) · also with ὑπό in tmesis: ’set beneath’ (ὑπὸ θρῆνυν … ἧκε ’set a footstool beneath’) · also with πρό in tmesis: ’sent forth’ (πρὸ … ἧκε)
ἧς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. gen. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whose, of whom/which (fem. gen. sg.)
ἰκαρίου: Ἰκάριος — Icarius, father of Penelope; masc. gen. sg.
ἰών: εἶμι — go; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἰὼν: εἶμι — go; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’going’
ἱστόν: ἱστός — loom; masc. acc. sg. · also ’mast’ (of a ship), a distinct sense required by nautical context (ἐν δ’ ἱστόν τ’ ἐτίθεντο ’they set the mast in it’)
ἱστὸν: ἱστός — loom, mast; masc. acc. sg. (here ’loom’, and by extension the web on it) · also ’mast’ (of a ship): ἱστὸν … στῆσαν ἀείραντες ’they raised and set up the mast’
ἴαυον: ἰαύω — sleep, lie down to sleep; impf. 3 pl. (the form also serves 1 sg.)
ἴλιον: Ἴλιος — Ilios, Troy; fem. acc. sg.
ἵκανεν: ἱκάνω — come upon, reach; impf./aor. 3 sg.
ἵκοντο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 pl.; with short ι (by metre) unaugmented; where the metre makes the ι long, augmented (the spelling cannot show it)
ὀδυσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. nom. sg., single-σ metrical variant Ὀδυσεύς
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσῆα: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. acc. sg., double-σ form (metrical variant of Ὀδυσῆα)
ὀδυσσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (double-σ, metrical variant of single-σ Ὀδυσῆος)
ὀδυσῆα: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; acc. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆα)
ὀδυσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆος)
ὀλοὴ: ὀλοός — deadly, destructive; fem. nom. sg.
ὀχῆας: ὀχεύς — bolt, bar; masc. acc. pl., epic -ῆας (= Attic ὀχέας)
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg. · also article-like with an adjective and a name: ’the’ (ὁ θρασὺς Ὀδυσσεύς ’bold Odysseus’) · also article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ὁ γέρων ’the old man’) · also distributive, masc. nom. sg.: ’the one’ (ὁ μὲν οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἱκάνει ’the one reaches the broad heaven’) · also article-like with a superlative: ’the worst’ (ὁ κάκιστος Ἀχαιῶν ’the worst of the Achaeans’)
ὃ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (relative) — who, which; neut. nom./acc. sg., referring to a person: ’that he...’ · also masc. nom. sg. relative, ’who’, used in address with a 2nd person verb (ὃ χθιζὸς θεὸς ἤλυθες ’you who came yesterday as a god’) · also pron. ’he’, masc. nom. sg. (ἧος ὃ … μιγείη) · also neut. acc. sg. relative, referring back to a thing, object of δῶκας: ’which (you gave me)’ · also = ὅτι ’that’, neut. acc. sg., introducing a clause after a verb of knowing (ὃ δὴ κακὰ μήδετο ’that evils were being devised’) · also neut. nom. sg. relative of a thing, subject of ἐστι: ’that which, whatever’ (ὃ κάλλιστον … ἐστι ’the one that is fairest’) · also neut. acc. sg. relative as a connective, ’for which reason, which is why’ (ὃ καὶ μεταμώνια βάζεις ’which is why you speak idly’)
ὄλβιε: ὄλβιος — prosperous, blessed; masc. voc. sg.
ὄληται: ὄλλυμαι — perish, be lost, be destroyed; aor. subj. 3 sg. mid. (μή + subj.: ’lest … perish’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’when … perishes’ (ἐπὴν … ὄληται) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὅπως: ’so that … may perish’
ὄρσας: ὄρνυμι — rouse, stir up; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having stirred up’
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron. (indefinite with τε/τις: ὅν τινα = ὅστις, ’whatever’); masc. acc. sg., accented before enclitic τινά · also plain relative pron., masc. acc. sg., not accented for a following enclitic: ’whom’ (ὅν ῥα καθεῖσεν ’whom he had stationed’)
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’) · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὅτε μέλλοι ’whenever he was about to’) · also with the pres. indic., ’whereas, when’ (ὅτε τ’ ἄλλοι ἅπαξ θνῄσκουσ’ ἄνθρωποι ’whereas other men die only once’) · also in ὅτε μή, ’unless, except when’ (ὅτε μὴ θεὸς … θείη ’unless a god should make’)
ὑπ: ὑπό (elided ὑπ’) — under, beneath; prep. + gen.; also + acc., ’under, up under’ · also of agent with a verb of dying, ‘by, at the hands of’ + gen. (ὤλεθ’ ὑπ’ Αἰγίσθοιο ‘perished by Aegisthus’) · also + dat., ’under, beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb, no case governed: οὓς ὑπ’ Ὀδυσσεὺς δύσετ’ = ὑπεδύσετο ’underneath which Odysseus sank down’
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat./acc.; also used as an adverb, ’beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis (ὑπὸ … ἐδήσατο = ὑπεδήσατο ’bound beneath’) · also adverbial, of breeding: ’begotten under, born of’ (ὑπὸ δ’ ἡμίονοι ’and under them [the mares], mules’) · also + dat., marking the agent with a passive verb: ’by’ (ὑπὸ μνηστῆρσιν δαμείη ’be overcome by the suitors’) · also + gen., ’from under, beneath’ (ὑπὸ στέρνοιο) · also + gen., marking agent with a passive verb/participle beyond dying, ’by’: μεγάλου ὑπὸ κύματος ἀρθείς ’lifted up by a great wave’ · also + gen., of cause: ὑπὸ ῥιπῆς ’at the rush (of the throw)’
ὑφαίνεσκεν: ὑφαίνω — weave; impf. 3 sg. iterative in -σκον
ὔμμ: σύ — you; pl. acc. ὔμμε, epic/Aeolic (= Attic ὑμᾶς), elided (ὔμμ’ = ὔμμε)
ὕφαινε: ὑφαίνω — weave; impf. 3 sg. (an augment on initial υ- does not show in writing)
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’) · also ὡς εἰ ’as if, like’ (ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα ’as if a wing or a thought’) · also ὡς + ἄν + opt., potential, ’as, in the way that, such as’ (ὡς οὐκ ἂν ἔλποιο ’such as you would not expect’) · also introducing a simile with the subj. and no ἄν: ’as when (a woman weeps)’ · also in an asseveration with fut. indic., ’as surely as’ (ὡς οὐκ ὀφθαλμόν γ’ ἰήσεται ’as surely as nothing will heal the eye’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. with a finite verb: ’how (dear) he is’ (ὡς ὅδε … φίλος … ἐστίν) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., of manner: ’as’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I shall say’) · also comparative ’like’, standing before its noun (ὡς νυκτερίς ’like a bat’) · also ὡς ὅθ’ (= ὡς ὅτε), ’as when’, comparing with an occasion in the past (ὡς ὅθ’ ὑπὸ Τροίην ’as when beneath Troy’) · also introducing an indirect statement after a verb of saying: ’that, how’ (εἴποιμ’ ὡς … ἔρχομαι ’I might tell how I am coming’) · also ὡς ἄν + opt., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἄν τίς σε … μακαρίζοι ’so that someone … would call you blessed’) · also ὡς + participle, ’as one who’ (ὡς ἐκ θανάτοιο φυγόντα ’as one escaped from death’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν … ἔρχησθον ’so that you two may go’) · also ὡς = ’to, toward’ + acc. of a person (ὡς τὸν ὁμοῖον ’to the like’) · also exclamatory ὡς + finite verb: ’how’ (ὡς ὁ μολοβρὸς … ἀγορεύει ’how the glutton talks’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’ · also introducing a wish with the optative: ’so may…’ (ὣς ἔμ’ ἀϊστώσειαν ’so may they make me vanish’)
ὤρνυτ: ὄρνυμι — stir, rouse; impf. mid. 3 sg., elided (ὤρνυτ’ = ὤρνυτο): ’rose’
ὧν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. gen. pl. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: of whom, whose; gen. pl., partitive (τοὺς δ’ ὧν ἐθέλει ’whomever he wishes’), not the possessive
ὧραι: ὥρα — season, time of year; fem. nom. pl.
ᾔδη: οἶδα — know; plpf. 3 sg. with past sense (= impf.): ’knew’
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥά: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, weak enclitic form ῥα, accented ῥά
ῥα: ἄρα — then, so; weak enclitic form ῥα (used after a vowel)
ῥηϊδίως: ῥηΐδιος — easy; adv. ῥηϊδίως: ’easily, readily’, epic (= Attic ῥᾳδίως)
